summary: Magdalene Geiger was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1911 and at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg in 1915. She was taught by Hermann Beckh, Heinrich Lüders, and Wilhelm Geiger.

Magdalene Sophie Schott was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at the universities of Tübingen, Münster, Berlin, Freiburg, and Marburg, and completed her Ph.D. under Max Walleser at Heidelberg University between 1928 and 1935.

Maggie Bickford is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology who studied at Bennington College, Yale University, and Princeton University. She served as Professor of East Asian Studies at Brown University in 1993 and was a Member at the Institute for Advanced Study around 1999–2000.

Mahadev Govind Ranade was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Elphinstone College, the University of Mumbai, and Government Law College, Mumbai, and went on to found the Maharashtra Girls Education Society in 1885.

Mahakachchakodiye Pangngasekara specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Sri Jayewardenepura between 2020 and 2023, and served as Senior Lecturer II at Bhiksu University of Sri Lanka from 2020 to 2024.
Mahala Rethlake works in Indology and religious studies. She has pursued a PhD in Religious Studies (Philosophy of Religions) as a doctoral candidate at the University of Chicago, attested in 2026.
Mahananda Timilsina is an Indologist who completed a PhD at Nepal Sanskrit University in 2015 and subsequently held an academic post there.

Maharshi Vyas is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. After studying as a PhD student at the University of California from 2017 to 2025, he became an Assistant Professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 2025.

Mahasi Sayadaw was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied under teachers including U Nārada, Aletawya Sayadaw, and Thelon Sayadaw. He served as abbot at Taung-waing-galay Taik Kyaung, taught at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha, and founded Insight Meditation Society.
Mahaveer H. Muhammad is a scholar in history, archaeology, linguistics, and Indology. He earned an M.A. from Shah Abdul Latif University and served as a researcher for the Government of Sindh.
Mahendradatta Jayadi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA in Buddhist Studies from International Buddhist College in 2013 and a Diploma in Pali from Somaiya Vidyavihar University in 2023.

Mahendranath Gupta was a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He was educated at Hare School, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta, and held professorial posts around 1885 at Ripon College and Surendranath College.

Mahesh A. Deokar is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who completed a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 2002. He became Head there in 2006 and has served as a Pali Text Society Regional Representative.

Mahesh Chandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University, with his tenure attested in 1882, 1894, and 1914.
Mahesh Kumar is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a BA Hons at Banaras Hindu University in 2020 and became a Research Scholar there in 2021.

Mahinda Deegalle is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Peradeniya, Harvard University, and the University of Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds, Wendy Doniger, and Diana L. Eck. He has held positions at Bath Spa, Cambridge, and SOAS.
Mahiro Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held professorships at Bukkyo University and Kyoto Bunkyo University, having succeeded Norihiko Tanaka in 2021.

Maho Iuchi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned a PhD from Otani University between 2003 and 2008 and was attested as a guest researcher at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies in 2010.
Mai Mishiro is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar whose posts include affiliations with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science in 2011 and Waseda University in 2016.

Makio Takemura is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned his degrees at the University of Tokyo and studied under Ryōmin Akizuki. He served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba and as president of Toyo University from 2009 to 2020.
